I agree that amount of potential is rediculous but for me, they killed it with the lazy warp drive. I get that they can't possibly render all those planets as well as all the space in between them but the incredibly short warp-drive absolutely ruined any sense of the universe's size for me. My and my brother have a minecraft world we've been working on for a long time and one of our proudest achievements is a railroad which connects two separate continents. But what's great about it is that it's incredibly long and the ride itself takes over 2 minutes. That might not sound like fin but the truth is, I love the sense of size and livelyness this grants our world. When I get in that cart and press the button I feel like I've set foot in a public train for a ride and the amount of time it takes really gives me a sense of actually being in another world, not just some rinky-dink simulation of a world. I don;t want to have to pilot the ship if I can't (though I'd love that), I don't want them to bust the bank for having to render all the space inbetween the planets, but if they would at least make the ride longer and maybe have the ship pass by some supernova remnants along the way that would, in my opinion, complete the expirience.

Really, all I want out of the game is to be able to fly from planet to planet in a spaceship. And seeing as there are like, a quadrillion planets, I expect I'll have fun with it.

Minecraft is really the only pure exploration game out there, it'll be nice to have an alternative.

I love the idea of constantly and procedurally rendering worlds, but I also wonder if it wouldn't be a bad idea for the game to include various catastrophic events in order to keep things fresh. For example, on a planet face lets say I discover a forest. Then lets say that there is a pre-scripted event that is set to happen at a certain time in the game's history in which an intelligent race removes my forest to make way for their city. My forest is no longer there, but that fact that I discovered it remains in the world's history. Then we can also have over events, such as entire planets being destroyed by their sun dying or an advanced race leaving their planet due to their sun dying and landing on a new one only to slaughter the intelligent life that lives their and destroying some of their cities and occupying others. See, if the game doesn't have motion like this, it will feel completely dead. A game of this size has to feel alive. If I discover a planet then leave and come back a long time later to find that nothing has changed, the universe won't end up being the immersive experience well all desire.

Of course, I can come up with ideas for days, buy I've got to accept that some will present more questions. In the case of this one, a question of time arises. If the games time moves at the same pace as real time (which, if it's an MMO, it has to) then how can these events realistically occur while everyone lives on at a normal pace. Stars don't die very often, afterall, and kingdoms usually take hundreds of years to rise and fall. So how do we solve this issue of in-game time? Honestly, if the game has no way of moving in this manner, then it sounds like it would be veery boring. Just discover something then watch nothing ever happen to it.

TL;DR:

  • I think the game should have catastrophic events which destroy things we've discovered to keep things moving.

  • If the game moves in real-time as an MMO, how would these things happen in a manner which is realistic to the time? Or should the time mechanics somehow be changed?

  • If the game doesn't include someway of keeping the world lively and moving, it will be VERY boring.
